classification.difficultyReason: Combine three corner-triangle area ratios to recover the outer area from the inner area.

content.prompt:
For $\triangle ABC$ shown below,
$$\begin{aligned}AD:DB&=1:1\\BE:EC&=3:7\\CF:FA&=1:2.\end{aligned}$$
Given that $\operatorname{area}(\triangle DEF)=5$, find $\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with horizontal AC and interior triangle DEF. Coordinates reconstruct the stated division ratios; they are not additional givens. The source cyan fill is intentionally omitted under the house outline convention.
spec.mathematics: D is the midpoint of AB; BE/BC=3/10; CF/CA=1/3. All six vertex labels and the three inner edges are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and labels are visible; no calculated area or solution annotation is included.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{300}{17}$ square units.

Subtract the three corner-triangle areas; $\triangle DEF$ occupies $\dfrac{17}{60}$ of $\triangle ABC$.
answer.worked:
Let $S=\operatorname{area}(\triangle ABC)$. Triangles sharing an included angle have area ratios equal to the products of the corresponding adjacent-side ratios.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(\triangle ADF)&=\frac{AD}{AB}\frac{AF}{AC}S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle ADF)&=\frac12\cdot\frac23S=\frac13S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle BDE)&=\frac{BD}{BA}\frac{BE}{BC}S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle BDE)&=\frac12\cdot\frac3{10}S=\frac3{20}S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle CEF)&=\frac{CE}{CB}\frac{CF}{CA}S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle CEF)&=\frac7{10}\cdot\frac13S=\frac7{30}S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle DEF)&=S-\frac13S-\frac3{20}S-\frac7{30}S\\\operatorname{area}(\triangle DEF)&=\frac{17}{60}S.\end{align*}$$
Since the inner area is 5,
$$\begin{align*}S&=5\cdot\frac{60}{17}\\S&=\frac{300}{17}\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$
